statement: Let Ω = (x−, x+) be bounded and let U ∈ H1 0 (Ω; Rn×d), where n, d ≥ 1, satisfy Z Ω UUT dx = In. For every δ, ε > 0 there are Cε ∈ Ln and Bε ∈ C1(Ω; Symn) such that, with Aε = CεU, εB′ ε = Mδ(Bε) − AεAT ε , Bε(x−) = K, Bε(x+) = −K. (B.15) They satisfy sup x∈Ω ∥Bε(x)∥op ≤ κ, sup 0<ε≤1 ∥Cε∥HS < ∞, (B.16) where the second bound is for fixed δ, K, Ω.
